As you know, a cure-temperature alarm appeared during the Tuesday night run on Press 8, so our standard process applies. I'll need the laboratory report on those 1,000 molded housings, and I'll also need a pallet-level traceability check confirming what's staged on pallets P1 through P4. Once I have both of those in hand, I can make my final disposition decision. Let's get started — what does the lab have for us so far?

transcript.text: Elena, I've completed a differential-scanning-calorimetry (DSC) review of the retained samples from Batch H-418 following the cure-temperature alarm. The results confirm that exactly 240 of the 1,000 housings are undercured. These 240 housings require a 4-hour thermal rework, and after rework, all 240 must undergo a hardness test before they can be released. I should note that my lab report is still awaiting final upload to the quality system — I'll get that completed shortly.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, I've completed the pallet-level serial lookup following the cure-temperature alarm. The results confirm that the 240 affected housings are exactly the 120 units on pallet P2 and the 120 units on pallet P3. Pallets P1 and P4 contain the remaining 760 unaffected housings. I haven't attached the lookup to the batch record yet because the disposition huddle hasn't been completed, but I'm providing it to you now for your disposition decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

decisions.disposition: Conditional release: Pallets P1 and P4 (760 unaffected housings) approved for shipment. Pallets P2 and P3 (240 affected housings) placed on hold for 4-hour thermal rework, followed by mandatory hardness testing on all 240 reworked units before release.
decisions.shipment_release_plan: Pallets P1 and P4 released immediately. Pallets P2 and P3 released only after completing 4-hour thermal rework and passing hardness testing on all 240 units. Lab report must be uploaded to the quality system and pallet-level traceability must be attached to the batch record before P2/P3 release.
